savePrompt.description: If true, the LLM prompt produced by the harness is included as a 'prompt' field on the action returned by core_harness, which causes it to be persisted in the episode replay. Defaults to false to keep replays small.

seed.description: Integer currently only used for selecting starting position.

strictMode.description: If true, agents must return only {'submission': int} (no extra fields like 'thoughts'), and per-agent TIMEOUT/ERROR/INVALID counts as a loss for the offending agent only — other agents win. If false (default), any agent error halts and voids the entire episode, matching the lenient research-mode behavior.

useImage.description: If true, indicates the observation is intended to be rendered as an image. Note that currently the agent harness is responsible for the actual rendering; no image is passed in the observation.

useOpenings.description: Whether to start from a position in an opening book.

currentPlayer.description: ID of player whose turn it is.

legalActionStrings.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action strings. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

legalActions.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action integers. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

openSpielGameName.description: Short name of the OpenSpiel game.

playerId.description: ID of the agent receiving this observation.

serializedGameAndState.description: Enables reconstructing the Game and State objects.

remainingOverageTime.description: Total remaining banked time (seconds) that can be used in excess of per-step actTimeouts -- agent is disqualified with TIMEOUT status when this drops below 0.

action.thoughts:
Reasoning:  
• The opponent (x) has opened with the strongest possible first move: the center column (column 3) at the bottom (row 5).  
• If we allow x to keep stacking in column 3, they can build an uncontested vertical threat and also gain maximum horizontal/diagonal reach from the central column.  
• By immediately playing our disk in the same column we both:
  – Block any future vertical connect-4 for x in that column.  
  – Occupy the most valuable column ourselves, giving us central control for future horizontal and diagonal lines.  
• Every other column leaves the center power square entirely in x’s hands, worsening our position.  
• Column 3 is legal (its top row is empty), and our disk will land on row 4.

Hence the optimal move is to drop in column 3.

Final Answer: 3

action.thoughts:
The current board has only two pieces placed, both in column 3: an x (my piece) at the bottom row and an o (opponent) directly above it. All other columns are completely empty, so any placement in columns 0-2 or 4-6 will land at the bottom row. 

No immediate win or threat is possible on this move, as I will only have two pieces total afterward. However, optimal play requires positioning for future connections (horizontal, diagonal, or vertical) while maintaining central control and creating potential double-threats (forks) that the opponent cannot fully block. 

Placing in column 3 is suboptimal: it drops my new x at row 3 in the same column, leaving my two x pieces separated by the opponent's o. This blocks any vertical connection and isolates my pieces, slowing down all possible lines. 

Instead, the strongest moves are in columns 2 or 4 (adjacent to my existing x at the bottom). This creates two connected x pieces at the bottom row, enabling rapid horizontal buildup. For example: 
- Playing in column 4 drops an x at the bottom of column 4. 
- If the opponent responds poorly (e.g., stacking on column 4), I can immediately extend to column 5 on my next turn to create three-in-a-row at the bottom with open spots on both ends (columns 2 and 6). The opponent can only block one, forcing a win on the following turn. 
- Even if the opponent plays optimally to prevent this (e.g., claiming column 5), I retain a strong central position with adjacent bottom pieces for ongoing threats and multiple line options. 

Column 2 is symmetric and equally strong. Columns 0, 1, 5, or 6 are weaker (too far from center and my existing piece, delaying connections). Column 3 is inferior as explained. 

I select column 4 as the optimal move for the reasons above. 

Final Answer: 4
